headline: South Asia: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack.
- Asia: Can Saudi Arabia’s 2034 Fifa World Cup survive the Middle East’s escalating wars?.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
The contract "supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat," Raytheon said.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Soldiers intervene on roadside to save children from alleged knife attack.
Three soldiers sprang into action when a highway crash in Washington turned into a knife attack on two children.
The Caribbean - bottom line: KIDD LANE  TERROR - Mom grieves for daughter who begged for help as triple murder rocks St Andrew community, forces residents to flee.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: KIDD LANE  TERROR - Mom grieves for daughter who begged for help as triple murder rocks St Andrew community, forces residents to flee.
The frantic voice of her daughter pleading for help over the telephone moments before she was killed will forever haunt Natasha Hall. Hall’s daughter, 30-year-old Lashane Ellis, and her one-year-old grandson, Kaheel Daley, were killed on Friday night when armed men went to their home on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, opened fire and set the house ablaze. Before fleeing, the gunmen reportedly opened fire on a neighbouring house, killing 39-year-old Kimeisha Gibson.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Search and rescue operations following a Russian guided bomb attack on a Zaporizhzhia residential building ended – 23 people have been killed, including four children.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russians strike two apartment blocks in Sloviansk: seven injured – photos, video.
Russian airstrikes hit two apartment blocks in Sloviansk, Donetsk Oblast, injuring seven people; Zelenskyy says residents may be trapped under rubble.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russian drone hits car in Sumy Oblast, killing driver.
Regional authorities have reported that a Russian drone attack killed a driver in a civilian car in the Krasnopillia hromada, Sumy Oblast, near the Russian border.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: One woman killed and ten people injured in Russian guided-bomb attack on Kharkiv.
A Russian guided bomb attack on a residential area in Kharkiv killed a 35-year-old woman, injured 10 others and destroyed two houses.

Dmytro Kuleba also said Ukraine will endure its worst winter yet as Russia targets the country's infrastructure in bid to break its resistance.
- Politico Europe, 15 hours ago: Russians face EU travel curbs to prevent hybrid attacks.
Tighter visa rules are expected to be proposed in January to bolster EU defenses against Russian threats.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 18 hours ago: Sudan: Drone Strikes and Deadly Explosions Kill Scores of Civilians Across Sudan.
[Dabanga] Wad El Mahi Locality / Geisan Locality / El Roseir -- Drone strikes and explosions have killed scores of civilians and injured dozens across Sudan, as attacks on displacement shelters and residential neighbourhoods in Blue Nile and North Kordofan coincide with deadly mine blasts in West Kordofan and renewed armed violence in South Darfur.
- Africanews, 6 hours ago: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine.
Zaporizhzhia was hit by deadly Russian airstrikes on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.
- Africanews, 4 hours ago: Eritrea uges United Nations to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia.
The neighbours have accused each other of starting a war over Tigray, where Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing rebels.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 18 hours ago: Ethiopia: UN Chief 'Gravely Concerned' By Renewed Fighting in Northern Ethiopia, Warns Against Escalation.
[UN News] UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called for an immediate end to the renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia, saying he is deeply worried by reports that Eritrean forces are present in the country.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack.
The Foreign Office (FO) on Sunday condemned a fresh wave of Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, reaffirming Pakistan’s “firm and unshakeable” commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Gulf state under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The defence pact, of which Turkiye is also a part, was signed on August 7 and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: KP Governor's Rule: An emergency in the street and state.
Back in 2024, the political future of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and perhaps of Pakistan itself, looked like a coin toss. There were two broad possibilities. One was a grand political settlement, perhaps involving a period of exile for Imran Khan, with the United Kingdom replacing Saudi Arabia as the preferred destination. The other was the eventual termination of the last PTI provincial government through constitutional intervention. One of these possibilities has now materialised.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Times of India - Top Stories, Jerusalem Post, Al Jazeera - Middle East, NDTV - Top Stories, Taipei Times, The Hindu - International, just now: New attack hits Riyadh airport, says Saudi coalition.
Riyadh airport came under fresh attack on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said, a day after a strike blamed on the group killed 12 people. Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said an unidentified projectile struck Terminal 4 at King Khalid International Airport, causing a fire, and that the relevant authorities were responding at the scene. He added in a post on X that air defences had “intercepted and destroyed” a cruise missile near the airport.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Soldier martyred, 12 terrorists killed as security forces foil infiltration attempt in Kurram: ISPR.
A soldier was martyred and 12 terrorists killed in an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kurram district, the army’s media wing said on Sunday. The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that the movement of a group of khawarij attempting to cross the international border from Afghanistan into Pakistan was detected in Kurram district on Sunday, where security forces engaged them effectively. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.
Asia - bottom line: Can Saudi Arabia’s 2034 Fifa World Cup survive the Middle East’s escalating wars?.
- South China Morning Post - China, 9 hours ago: Can Saudi Arabia’s 2034 Fifa World Cup survive the Middle East’s escalating wars?.
When 60,000 football fans gathered in Jeddah for the Arabian Gulf Cup on Tuesday, they inadvertently highlighted the vulnerability of major sports events hosted by Gulf monarchies to the wars raging across the region. The previous day, Saudi Arabia resumed strikes on Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthi rebels after a four-year ceasefire collapsed. That truce had originally followed a Houthi attack on an oil facility near Jeddah’s Formula One track during a practice session. While the two-week football...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Trump says Russia, Ukraine agree to ‘energy ceasefire’.
US President Donald Trump said in a brief statement on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt strikes on each other’s energy infrastructure, prompting surprise from Ukraine’s leader, who said the announcement was “news for me”. There was no immediate comment from Russia on Trump’s claim. Russia has launched waves of attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure since invading in February 2022, knocking out power and heating to millions during freezing temperatures, while Ukraine has...
- South China Morning Post - China, 7 hours ago: How Taiwan’s military manpower shortage is undermining its ability to fight.
Taiwan’s military is grappling with a worsening manpower shortage, with its volunteer staffing rate remaining below the 80 per cent target for a third consecutive year and concerns mounting over the impact on combat readiness, according to the island’s legislature. The shortages extend deep into frontline formations – including infantry, artillery, missile and air defence units – raising questions over whether Taiwan will have enough trained personnel to operate and maintain the vast quantities...
- South China Morning Post - China, 11 hours ago: Spirit of Hong Kong Awards: Gaza nurse’s obstacle-laden road to becoming a professor.
On six occasions, Hammoda Abu-Odah, a Gaza nurse-turned Hong Kong scholar was offered an opportunity to study overseas. But each time, border closures and travel restrictions prevented him from taking them up. Abu-Odah had obtained a nursing degree in his native Gaza but set his sights on an academic career abroad. He kept working, teaching and conducting research, despite the many challenges that prevented him from leaving. Finally, on the seventh attempt, he made it to Hong Kong, where he...

- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: One Indian killed, 10 injured in Riyadh airport strike; chilling video shows aftermath.

Nuclear war and the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) could put the future of humanity at risk, a new report stated.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Couple rejects $131,000 offer for data center power line on their property.
Jerry Zelenka has turned down American Transmission Company's proposal to place a power line on his property, citing worries over tree removal and the demolition of numerous buildings. He is particularly troubled by the level of compensation offered and the potential threat of eminent domain. Meanwhile, legal disputes from neighboring landowners about the project's validity persist.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Florida family protects 498-acre cattle ranch in $7.48m conservation deal.
A 498-acre cattle ranch known as Turnpike Dairy has been protected from future development through a conservation easement. The agreement allows the managing family to continue agricultural operations on the property. Martin County contributed $3.74 million towards the $7.48 million deal to preserve the land. This conservation effort is part of Florida’s Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, which protects working farms.
